chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Umar ibn Hanzala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Beware of the women who are divorced three times in one sitting, for they are considered to have one husband.

key_terms.ذَوَاتُ أَزوَاجٍ: Possessors of husbands (implying the bond remains)

ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one sitting make the divorce final and irrevocable in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar highlights the Shia juristic view that triple divorce pronounced in a single session counts as only one revocable divorce (talaq raj'i), allowing the couple to reconcile without a new marriage contract after the waiting period. This contrasts with the Sunni majority opinion which often treats it as irrevocable, reflecting the Shia interpretation of Quranic verses regarding the number of divorces. The ruling emphasizes the procedural integrity of the divorce process, ensuring that the 'three' divorces are not merely a formulaic utterance but carry specific legal weight.
